name: LiF rocksalt (NBS measured26°C)
citation: H. E. Swanson and E. Tatge (1953). Standard X-ray Diffraction Powder Patterns. National Bureau of Standards Circular539,Volume1,issued June15,1953. pp61–62,Table35.
derivation: Locally authored CIF transcribed from original measured NBS lattice and its explicitly stated NaCl-type structural model.
conditions_evidence: Table35 explicitly labels26°C; general measurement protocol states temperature remained within±1°C of the stated table value. Numeric pressure was not specified. The p61 comparison converts to25°C and is not used here.
method: Experimental NBS powder X-ray diffraction with CuKalpha wavelength1.5405Å and internal tungsten standard.
synthesis_conditions_note: Commercial sample supplied by Harshaw; no growth temperature or pressure inferred.
selection: Experimental NBS lattice and published rocksalt symmetry, explicitly transcribed; not a theoretical relaxation, substituted prototype, or original COD file.
notes: No independent atomic-coordinate or occupancy refinement is claimed. Fm-3m rocksalt has fixed special-position coordinates and unit-occupancy stoichiometry; this encoding represents the published model.
Trace impurities reported by NBS are not represented as substitutions.
No lattice standard uncertainty is given with the selected mean; retained digits are not an invented error bar.

Low-energy light-element K-edge FEFF paths are unvalidated candidate scattering references, not a demonstration of usable measured EXAFS or XANES accuracy. Core excitons, band structure, charge transfer and nonspherical potentials can matter near these edges; retain actual SCF convergence, potential and executable diagnostics.

A nominal native k grid is not an experimental usable k range. Choose an absorber/edge-appropriate measured range and validate against data; a converged FEFF calculation alone does not validate this reference.

license.status: Locally authored transcription of numeric crystallographic facts from a US National Bureau of Standards government report, with full attribution. This is not a COD artifact.
license.note: The raw NBS report is available from the NIST government archive. No journal PDF is included; the standalone CIF and transcription metadata are the source deliverable.

inspection.occupancy_evidence: Unit occupancies encode the published stoichiometric NaCl-type model; they are not independently refined occupancies.

Coexisting F K edge (696.7 eV) lies above Li K (54.7 eV), at nominal k=12.981 A^-1. Its absorption/background can interfere with measured Li spectra; this atomic-energy landmark is not an automatic usable-k limit.
